## Overview

Lecture 1 built the Carhart benchmark and warned that **alpha is only as good as the model**. Lecture 2 asked whether the alpha that survives is skill or luck. Both lectures took one thing for granted: that we already know **which funds are in the sample, what kind of funds they are, and whether each fund stays the same kind of fund over time**. In empirical work on mutual funds, that assumption is where many results are won or lost.

This lecture therefore studies the front end of every fund study, in three steps:

1.  **Clean the sample.** The CRSP Survivor-Bias-Free US Mutual Fund Database is not a random draw of funds. Incubation, tiny funds, share classes, and mislabeled products all push estimates in predictable directions. We follow the sample filters of @dannhauser2026, @doshi2015, and @back2018 and show *why* each filter exists.
2.  **Classify the funds.** Who is an *active* equity fund, an *index* fund, or an *ETF*? We compare three published recipes — @doshi2015, @back2018, and @dannhauser2026 — on the same data.
3.  **Study style and style drift.** What is a fund's investment style, where do style labels come from, and what happens when a fund's style moves? The key paper is @chan2002: we report their findings, then rebuild their design on simulated funds to see what it can and cannot detect.

::: callout-note
## What moved out of this lecture

Benchmark selection and Active Share, which the earlier draft of this lecture covered, move to a later lecture. They need the clean sample and the style infrastructure built here.
:::

By the end of the lecture, you should be able to:

- explain the unit-of-observation problem in CRSP (share class vs. fund) and aggregate share classes correctly;
- explain, with a simulation, how incubation bias manufactures "skilled" managers;
- apply and compare three classification recipes and diagnose their failure modes (name-parsing false positives, sector funds, hedged funds);
- distinguish *stated* style from *revealed* style, and measure style drift both ways;
- summarize the evidence in @chan2002 on style consistency and on who changes style, and explain why a rank-based drift measure has a noise floor and a mechanical winner-loser gap;
- interactively explore the results: every figure in this handout is a `highcharter` chart you can hover, zoom, and toggle.

### 1.1 Where does the fund data come from?

The CRSP Mutual Fund Database is licensed, so a public handout cannot ship it, and the results of this lecture cannot be shown on real CRSP data. Every chunk below therefore runs on a **simulated CRSP-style panel** with the same column names as the CRSP fund summary file (`crsp_fundno`, `wficn`, `lipper_obj_cd`, `crsp_obj_cd`, `index_fund_flag`, `et_flag`, `tna_latest`, `exp_ratio`, and so on). If you have WRDS access, the same code runs on your own extract once you replace `simulate_crsp()` with a loader that returns these columns.

Simulated data have one advantage that real data never have: we **know the true type of every fund**, so we can score each filter and each classification recipe against the truth.

::: callout-tip
## Caching

Chunk results are cached (`cache: true`). If you change the simulator or its seed, render once with `quarto render --cache-refresh` so that cached chunks are rebuilt.
:::

The simulator builds portfolios of twelve true types, spins each into one to four share classes, lets styles drift, blanks out some codes, and plants the data problems we will filter later. It is long, but the point of the lecture is what happens *after* it; skim it.

```{r}
#| label: simulate

simulate_crsp <- function(n_port = 1500, seed = 2026) {
  set.seed(seed)

  # --- vendor style codes for broad domestic-equity funds (illustrative) ------
  broad <- tribble(
    ~lipper_obj_cd, ~lipper_class, ~si_obj_cd, ~wbrger_obj_cd, ~crsp_obj_cd,
    "G",  "LCGE", "GRO", "G",   "EDYG",
    "GI", "LCCE", "GRI", "GCI", "EDYB",
    "EI", "EIEI", "ING", "IEQ", "EDYI",
    "MC", "MCGE", "GMC", "MCG", "EDCM",
    "SG", "SCGE", "SCG", "SCG", "EDCS",
    "CA", "MLGE", "AGG", "LTG", "EDYG",
    "MR", "MLCE", "GRO", "IEQ", "EDCM"
  ) |> mutate(sid = row_number())

  sector <- tribble(
    ~lipper_obj_cd, ~lipper_class, ~si_obj_cd, ~wbrger_obj_cd, ~crsp_obj_cd, ~sector_name,
    "TK", "SPTK", "SEC", "S", "EDSF", "Technology",
    "H",  "SPHE", "SEC", "S", "EDSH", "Health Sciences",
    "FS", "SPFS", "SEC", "S", "EDSN", "Financial Services",
    "RE", "SPRE", "SEC", "S", "EDSR", "Real Estate",
    "UT", "SPUT", "SEC", "S", "EDSU", "Wind Energy"
  ) |> mutate(sid = row_number()) |> rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_s"), -sid)

  type_lvls <- c("active_broad", "active_sector", "active_special",
                 "active_foreign_name", "index", "etf_index", "etf_active",
                 "etn", "enhanced", "target", "intl", "bond")
  type_prob <- c(.38, .07, .03, .02, .09, .05, .02, .01, .02, .06, .13, .12)

  families <- c("Alder", "Beacon", "Cedar", "Delta", "Everest",
                "Falcon", "Granite", "Harbor", "Juniper", "Kestrel")

  style_path <- function(n, k, p_switch = 0.04) {
    s <- integer(n); s[1] <- sample(k, 1)
    for (i in seq_len(n)[-1]) s[i] <- if (runif(1) < p_switch) sample(k, 1) else s[i - 1]
    s
  }

  # --- portfolios -------------------------------------------------------------
  port <- tibble(
    wficn     = 1:n_port,
    true_type = sample(type_lvls, n_port, TRUE, type_prob),
    family    = sample(families, n_port, TRUE)
  ) |>
    mutate(
      first_year = map_int(true_type, \(t) {
        lo <- switch(t, etf_index = , etf_active = , etn = 2000L, index = 1990L, 1985L)
        sample(lo:2022L, 1, prob = (lo:2022L) - lo + 5)   # launches grow over time
      }),
      last_year    = pmin(2023L, first_year + 2L + rgeom(n(), 0.07)),
      no_codes     = runif(n()) < 0.03,                   # some funds never carry a style code
      special_kind = sample(1:3, n(), TRUE),
      tdf_eq_code  = runif(n()) < 0.40,
      idx_flagged  = runif(n()) < 0.70,
      base_tna     = exp(rnorm(n(), 4.5, 1.8)),            # $ millions
      offer_month  = sample(1:12, n(), TRUE),
      first_offer  = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-15", first_year, offer_month)),
      name_pick    = sample(1:11, n(), TRUE),
      trap_pick    = runif(n())
    ) |>
    filter(last_year >= 2000L)

  # --- fund names (with a few planted traps) ------------------------------------
  act_words <- c("Growth", "Value Opportunities", "Capital Appreciation", "Mid Cap",
                 "Small Cap", "Equity Income", "Blue Chip", "Dividend Growth",
                 "Select", "Contrarian", "Core")
  port <- port |>
    mutate(
      base_name = case_when(
        true_type == "active_broad" ~ paste(family, act_words[name_pick], "Fund"),
        true_type == "active_special" ~ paste(family, c("Market Neutral", "Short Alpha", "Covered Call")[special_kind], "Fund"),
        true_type == "active_foreign_name" ~ paste(family, c("China", "India", "Japan", "Asia", "Europe")[name_pick %% 5 + 1], "Opportunities Fund"),
        true_type == "index" ~ paste(family, c("500 Index", "Total Market Index", "Small Cap Index", "Value Index", "Growth Index", "Extended Market Index", "Russell 1000 Index", "Mid Cap Index", "Large Cap Idx", "Equity Index", "Total Stock Indx")[name_pick], "Fund"),
        true_type == "etf_index" ~ paste(family, c("Core S&P 500 ETF", "Total Market ETF", "Small Cap ETF", "Large Cap ETF", "Dividend ETF")[name_pick %% 5 + 1]),
        true_type == "etf_active" ~ paste(family, c("Active Growth ETF", "Active Value ETF", "Dynamic Equity ETF")[name_pick %% 3 + 1]),
        true_type == "etn" ~ paste(family, "Leveraged Energy ETN"),
        true_type == "enhanced" ~ paste(family, c("Ultra Equity", "2x Large Cap", "Enhanced Equity", "Equity Plus")[name_pick %% 4 + 1], "Fund"),
        true_type == "target" ~ paste(family, "Retirement", seq(2010, 2060, 5)[name_pick], "Fund"),
        true_type == "intl" ~ paste(family, c("International", "Global", "Emerging Markets", "World")[name_pick %% 4 + 1], "Fund"),
        true_type == "bond" ~ paste(family, c("Core Bond", "High Yield", "Municipal Bond")[name_pick %% 3 + 1], "Fund"),
        TRUE ~ paste(family, "Fund")
      ),
      # traps: names that fool naive substring rules
      base_name = if_else(true_type == "active_broad" & trap_pick < 0.04, paste(family, "Growth Fund RSP"), base_name),
      base_name = if_else(true_type == "active_broad" & trap_pick > 0.97, paste(family, "Select 100 Opportunities Fund"), base_name)
    )

  # --- share classes ----------------------------------------------------------------
  cls <- port |>
    mutate(n_cls = sample(1:4, n(), TRUE, c(.35, .30, .20, .15))) |>
    uncount(n_cls, .id = "k") |>
    mutate(crsp_fundno = 10000L + row_number(),
           crsp_cl_grp = 500000L + wficn,
           crsp_portno = if_else(runif(n()) < .8, 8000L + wficn, NA_integer_),
           w_cls       = c(.50, .30, .15, .05)[k]) |>
    mutate(class_share = w_cls / sum(w_cls), .by = wficn) |>
    select(wficn, k, crsp_fundno, crsp_cl_grp, crsp_portno, class_share)

  # --- portfolio-year panel with style paths ------------------------------------------
  pp <- port |>
    mutate(year = map2(pmax(first_year, 2000L), last_year, \(a, b) a:b)) |>
    unnest(year) |>
    mutate(style_id = style_path(n(), 7L,
                                 if (first(true_type) %in% c("active_broad", "active_special", "active_foreign_name")) 0.04 else 0),
           .by = wficn) |>
    mutate(sid = style_id, sid_s = ((style_id - 1L) %% 5L) + 1L) |>
    left_join(broad,  by = "sid") |>
    left_join(sector, by = c("sid_s" = "sid"))

  pp <- pp |>
    mutate(
      equity_coded = true_type %in% c("active_broad", "active_special", "active_foreign_name",
                                      "index", "etf_index", "etf_active", "etn", "enhanced") |
                     (true_type == "target" & tdf_eq_code),
      lipper_obj_cd = case_when(true_type == "active_sector" ~ lipper_obj_cd_s,
                                equity_coded ~ lipper_obj_cd,
                                true_type == "intl" ~ "IL", true_type == "bond" ~ "A",
                                TRUE ~ "MTD"),
      lipper_class  = case_when(true_type == "active_sector" ~ lipper_class_s,
                                equity_coded ~ lipper_class, TRUE ~ "OTHR"),
      si_obj_cd     = case_when(true_type == "active_sector" ~ si_obj_cd_s,
                                true_type == "active_special" & special_kind == 3L ~ "OPI",
                                equity_coded ~ si_obj_cd, TRUE ~ "OTH"),
      wbrger_obj_cd = case_when(true_type == "active_sector" ~ wbrger_obj_cd_s,
                                equity_coded ~ wbrger_obj_cd, TRUE ~ "OTH"),
      crsp_obj_cd   = case_when(true_type == "active_sector" ~ crsp_obj_cd_s,
                                true_type == "active_special" ~ c("EDYH", "EDYS", "EDYI")[special_kind],
                                equity_coded ~ crsp_obj_cd,
                                true_type == "intl" ~ "EICE", true_type == "bond" ~ "ICQY",
                                TRUE ~ "MTAL"),
      base_name = if_else(true_type == "active_sector",
                          paste(family, sector_name_s, "Fund"), base_name),
      age_y     = year - first_year,
      index_fund_flag = case_when(
        year < 2008 ~ NA_character_,
        true_type == "index" & idx_flagged ~ sample(c("D", "B"), n(), TRUE),
        true_type == "etf_index" ~ "D",
        true_type == "enhanced" ~ "E",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      et_flag = case_when(true_type %in% c("etf_index", "etf_active") ~ "F",
                          true_type == "etn" ~ "N", TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      tna_port  = base_tna * exp(0.08 * pmin(pmax(age_y, 0), 20) + rnorm(n(), 0, .25))
    )

  blank <- function(x, p) if_else(runif(length(x)) < p, "", x)

  pp |>
    inner_join(cls, by = "wficn", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    mutate(
      class_suffix = c("A", "C", "I", "Admiral")[k],
      fund_name    = paste0(base_name, ";", class_suffix),
      caldt        = as.Date(sprintf("%d-12-31", year)),
      first_offer_dt = first_offer + (k - 1L) * 180L,
      tna_latest   = if_else(runif(n()) < 0.02, NA_real_, tna_port * class_share),
      er_mean      = case_when(str_detect(true_type, "^active") ~ .0115,
                               true_type == "index" ~ .0020,
                               str_detect(true_type, "^etf") ~ .0040, TRUE ~ .0100),
      exp_ratio    = pmax(.0005, rnorm(n(), er_mean, er_mean / 3) + c(0, .0075, 0, -.003)[k]),
      exp_ratio    = case_when(runif(n()) < .02  ~ -99,
                               runif(n()) < .005 ~ .15,
                               runif(n()) < .01  ~ NA_real_, TRUE ~ exp_ratio),
      across(c(lipper_obj_cd, crsp_obj_cd), \(x) blank(x, .06)),
      across(c(lipper_class, si_obj_cd, wbrger_obj_cd), \(x) blank(x, .25)),
      across(c(lipper_obj_cd, lipper_class, si_obj_cd, wbrger_obj_cd, crsp_obj_cd),
             \(x) if_else(no_codes, "", x))
    ) |>
    select(crsp_fundno, crsp_cl_grp, crsp_portno, wficn, fund_name, year, caldt,
           first_offer_dt, tna_latest, exp_ratio, lipper_class, lipper_obj_cd,
           si_obj_cd, wbrger_obj_cd, crsp_obj_cd, index_fund_flag, et_flag, true_type)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data

fund_raw <- simulate_crsp(n_port = 1500, seed = 2026)

fund_raw <- fund_raw |> filter(!is.na(tna_latest))   # require non-missing TNA

cat("Data source: simulated CRSP-style panel", "\n",
    "Share-class-years:", format(nrow(fund_raw), big.mark = ","), "\n",
    "Share classes:    ", format(n_distinct(fund_raw$crsp_fundno), big.mark = ","), "\n",
    "Funds (WFICN):    ", format(n_distinct(fund_raw$wficn), big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

## 2. The Unit of Observation: Share Class vs. Fund

A "fund" in CRSP is not one row. Most funds sell several **share classes** (A, C, institutional, ...) that hold the same portfolio and differ only in fees and target clients. CRSP gives each share class its own identifier, and a handful of other identifiers sit above it.

| Identifier | Level | Use |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `crsp_fundno` | Share class | Fees, loads, 12b-1 fees, and TNA differ by share class |
| `crsp_cl_grp` | Class group | CRSP's grouping of share classes of the same fund |
| `crsp_portno` | Portfolio | Links to holdings; not populated for every share class |
| `wficn` | Fund | MFLINKS identifier that links CRSP to Thomson Reuters holdings |

: CRSP fund identifiers

If we treat each share class as a fund, a fund with four share classes counts four times in every cross-section, and its alpha is counted four times in a skill test. The standard fix, used by @doshi2015, @back2018, and @dannhauser2026, is to **aggregate share classes to the portfolio level**: TNA is summed, fund age is the age of the *oldest* share class, and all other characteristics (expense ratio, turnover) are **TNA-weighted** averages.

```{r}
#| label: toy-aggregation

toy <- tribble(
  ~class, ~first_offer_dt,  ~tna,  ~exp_ratio,
  "A",    "2004-03-15",     600,   0.0115,
  "C",    "2006-09-15",     150,   0.0190,
  "I",    "2009-01-15",     250,   0.0085
) |> mutate(first_offer_dt = as.Date(first_offer_dt))

toy_fund <- toy |>
  summarise(
    total_tna        = sum(tna),
    fund_first_offer = min(first_offer_dt),                 # oldest share class
    er_tna_weighted  = weighted.mean(exp_ratio, tna),
    er_simple_mean   = mean(exp_ratio)
  )

toy_fund |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = total_tna, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(er_tna_weighted, er_simple_mean), decimals = 4) |>
  cols_label(total_tna = "Fund TNA ($M)", fund_first_offer = "Fund first offer date",
             er_tna_weighted = "Expense ratio (TNA-weighted)",
             er_simple_mean = "Expense ratio (simple mean)") |>
  tab_header(title = "Aggregating Three Share Classes into One Fund",
             subtitle = "The simple mean overstates the fee that the average dollar pays")
```

The simple mean over-weights the expensive, small share class. The TNA-weighted average is what the *average dollar invested in the fund actually pays*.

## 3. Why Filter? Cleaning the CRSP Sample

A raw CRSP extract is *not* a sample of "equity mutual funds". It also contains bond funds, international funds, target-date funds, tiny funds, funds in their private incubation period, and funds with missing or nonsensical fields. Each of the papers below applies a short list of filters before computing anything. The filters look like housekeeping, but each one removes a specific, documented bias.

### 3.1 The Filters and Why They Exist

| Filter | Rule (paper) | Why |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **Incubation / backfill** | Drop the first 18 months of returns [@doshi2015]; only use returns after the first offer date and when the fund name is non-missing [@back2018]; drop the first 3 years of a fund's life [@dannhauser2026] | Funds incubated privately are opened to the public only after good results [@evans2010] |
| **Small funds** | Drop fund-periods with TNA below \$15 million [@doshi2015; @back2018; @dannhauser2026] | Returns of very small funds are noisy and, as @elton2001 show, biased upward in CRSP |
| **Equity share** | Drop funds that on average hold less than 80% of assets in equity [@doshi2015, following @kacperczyk2008] | Objective codes do not always describe what the fund really holds |
| **Too few holdings** | Drop observations with ten or fewer stock holdings [@doshi2015; @back2018] | Holdings-based measures become meaningless |
| **Missing name** | Drop funds with missing names [@doshi2015] | Names are needed for classification; missing names also flag backfilled periods [@back2018] |
| **Missing fields** | Drop observations with missing returns or expense ratio [@dannhauser2026]; require at least 60 days of returns and at least 90% non-missing daily returns [@back2018] | Reporting irregularities (for example weekly-reporting funds) |
| **Not domestic equity** | Keep CRSP objective codes starting with `ED` or the listed Lipper codes; drop China, Brazil, India, Europe, Asia, or Japan in the name [@dannhauser2026] | Different asset class or mandate |
| **Special products** | Drop target-date funds [@parker2023], ETNs, leveraged and inverse funds, funds of funds, and active ETFs [@dannhauser2026] | Different mandate; not comparable with plain-vanilla funds |
| **Consistency** | Require a fund to meet its type definition in at least 50% of its observations [@dannhauser2026] | Avoids funds flagged as index for just 2% of their history |

: Sample filters used in the three papers

Three of these filters need data beyond the fund summary table: the 80% equity-share rule and the ten-holdings rule need holdings data (Thomson Reuters S12 or N-PORT), and the daily-return rules need the daily returns file. The pipeline in §3.3 implements the filters that can be applied to the summary table.

### 3.2 Incubation Bias: A Simulation

@evans2010 documents the mechanism. A fund family starts several funds **privately**, often funded by the family itself, and tracks their results. After an evaluation period it opens only *some* of them to the public. The funds that are opened are, by construction, the ones that did well. Evans finds that incubated funds outperform non-incubated funds by roughly 3.5% on a risk-adjusted basis, that the outperformance disappears after the fund goes public, and that this inflates reported returns. A fund-size filter does not remove the bias, but fund-age and ticker-creation-date filters do.

We simulate the mechanism with **zero skill**: every fund's true alpha is exactly zero.

```{r}
#| label: incubation-sim

set.seed(2026)
n_fam <- 200; k <- 8                # 200 families, each incubates 8 private funds
T_inc <- 36; T_pub <- 60            # 36 private months, then 60 public months
sd_m  <- 0.018                      # monthly idiosyncratic volatility
release_share <- 0.25               # the best quarter of incubated funds are opened

# Incubated funds: monthly abnormal returns, true alpha = 0
inc <- expand_grid(family = 1:n_fam, fund = 1:k, age = 1:(T_inc + T_pub)) |>
  mutate(fid = paste(family, fund, sep = "-"),
         ar  = rnorm(n(), 0, sd_m))

# The family opens the funds with the best incubation record
released <- inc |>
  filter(age <= T_inc) |>
  summarise(cum_inc = sum(ar), .by = c(family, fund, fid)) |>
  mutate(rk = rank(-cum_inc), .by = family) |>
  filter(rk <= ceiling(release_share * k)) |>
  pull(fid)

inc_rel <- inc |> filter(fid %in% released) |> mutate(group = "Incubated, then opened")

# Comparison funds: never incubated, listed from their first month
n_ctrl <- 3 * length(released)
ctrl <- expand_grid(fund = 1:n_ctrl, age = 1:(T_inc + T_pub)) |>
  mutate(fid = paste0("c", fund), ar = rnorm(n(), 0, sd_m), group = "Not incubated")

sim_funds <- bind_rows(inc_rel, ctrl) |> select(group, fid, age, ar)

cat("Incubated funds opened:", length(released), "of", n_fam * k, "\n",
    "Never-incubated funds: ", n_ctrl, "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-incubation
#| fig-cap: "Average cumulative abnormal return by fund age: incubated funds look skilled only while they are private"

cum_path <- sim_funds |>
  arrange(group, fid, age) |>
  mutate(cum_ar = cumsum(ar), .by = c(group, fid)) |>
  summarise(mean_cum = mean(cum_ar) * 100, .by = c(group, age))

hchart(cum_path, "line", hcaes(x = age, y = mean_cum, group = group)) |>
  hc_chart(zoomType = "x", height = 420) |>
  hc_title(text = "True alpha is zero for every fund") |>
  hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Fund age (months)"),
           plotLines = list(list(value = T_inc, color = "#444444", width = 1,
                                 dashStyle = "Dash", zIndex = 3,
                                 label = list(text = "Fund opens to the public",
                                              rotation = 0, y = 12, x = 6)))) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Mean cumulative abnormal return (%)"),
           labels = list(format = "{value}%")) |>
  hc_tooltip(shared = TRUE, valueDecimals = 2, valueSuffix = "%") |>
  hc_plotOptions(series = list(lineWidth = 2, marker = list(enabled = FALSE)))
```

The released funds climb steadily while private, because the family selected them on that very record. Once the fund is open, the line goes flat: the selection effect is gone, and the true alpha of zero is visible. The never-incubated funds are flat throughout.

Why this matters: if the database backfills the private record into the fund's history and we use it, a pooled estimate is biased upward and "skilled" managers appear. We can measure both effects in the simulation.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-incubation
#| tbl-cap: "Incubation bias: pooled alpha and false 'skilled' funds, before and after the age filter"

eval_sample <- function(d, label) {
  fund_stats <- d |>
    summarise(m = mean(ar), s = sd(ar), n = n(), .by = c(group, fid)) |>
    mutate(t = m / (s / sqrt(n)))
  inc_only <- d$group == "Incubated, then opened"
  tibble(sample = label,
         `Pooled alpha (% per year)`          = mean(d$ar) * 1200,
         `Incubated funds only (% per year)`  = mean(d$ar[inc_only]) * 1200,
         `Funds with t > 1.96 (%)`            = mean(fund_stats$t > 1.96) * 100,
         `... incubated funds only (%)`       = mean(fund_stats$t[fund_stats$group == "Incubated, then opened"] > 1.96) * 100)
}

bind_rows(
  eval_sample(sim_funds, "No filter (backfilled history included)"),
  eval_sample(filter(sim_funds, age > T_inc), "Drop first 36 months of every fund")
) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = 2:5, decimals = 2) |>
  tab_header(title = "Same Funds, Same Returns, Different Conclusions",
             subtitle = "True alpha = 0 for every fund; a one-sided 5% test should flag about 2.5% by luck") |>
  tab_source_note("Illustrative simulation; parameters are chosen for visibility, not calibrated to CRSP.")
```

Without the filter, the incubated funds show a sizeable positive alpha and several times the luck rate of statistically "skilled" funds, even though every fund has zero true alpha. The pooled alpha is smaller because only a quarter of the simulated funds were incubated, but it is still visibly positive. With the age filter, both alphas fall to roughly zero and the share of "skilled" funds returns to the luck rate. (The remaining differences from exactly zero are sampling noise.) This connects directly to Lecture 2: incubation bias is a *selection* problem, so it feeds the false discoveries that the luck-versus-skill tests are designed to count.

::: callout-important
**Three papers, three versions of the same fix.** @doshi2015 drop 18 months, @back2018 use the first offer date and the name-availability date, and @dannhauser2026 drop three years (which also removes the burst of newly launched ETFs that cater to investor sentiment, see @bendavid2023). The longer the window, the safer the filter, and the more young funds you lose. This is a design choice that you should report and test for robustness.
:::

### 3.3 The Filter Pipeline, Step by Step

We now apply the filters that can be applied to the fund summary table and **record how many funds survive each step**. First, the helpers and the classification flags used in the pipeline (they are explained in §4).

```{r}
#| label: helpers

blank_to_na <- function(x) if_else(x == "", NA_character_, x)
mode_chr    <- function(x) {                        # most frequent non-missing value
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
}

# ---- Dannhauser & Pontiff (2026) parameters ---------------------------------
dp_lipper  <- c("CA", "EI", "G", "GI", "MC", "MR", "SG", "SP", "BM", "CG", "CS",
                "FS", "H", "ID", "N", "RE", "TK", "TL", "S", "UT")
dp_foreign <- "china|brazil|india|europe|asia|japan"
dp_index_names <- paste0("index|idx|indx|ind |composite|russell|s&p|s and p|s & p|",
                         "msci|bloomberg|kbw|nasdaq|nyse|stoxx|ftse|wilshire|",
                         "morningstar|100|400|500|600|900|1000|1500|2000|3000|5000")
dp_etf_names   <- "etf|ishares|spdr|holdrs|streettracks|exchange traded|exchange-traded"
dp_enh_names   <- "plus|enhanced|inverse|bull|bear|2x|3x|ultra|1\\.5x|2\\.5x"

# ---- Target-date funds (Parker, Schoar, and Sun 2023): name contains a vintage
identify_tdf <- function(x, year) {
  # a year, but not when it follows "Russell" or "Russ" (the Russell 2000 index)
  td <- if_else(str_detect(x, sprintf("(?<!Russell ?|Russ ?)%i", year)), 1, 0)
  td <- if_else(str_detect(x, sprintf("%i\\+|V%i|AXA Tactical|AXA %i|%i ETF|Focused %i Value",
                                      year, year, year, year, year)), 1, td)
  td
}

flag_types <- function(d) {
  d |>
    mutate(
      name_lc = str_to_lower(coalesce(fund_name, "")),

      # Step 1 of DP (2026): domestic-equity universe
      domestic_equity =
        (coalesce(str_starts(crsp_obj_cd, "ED"), FALSE) | lipper_obj_cd %in% dp_lipper) &
        !str_detect(name_lc, dp_foreign),

      # Passive funds: CRSP index flag D or B, or a name match
      index_fund = coalesce(index_fund_flag %in% c("D", "B"), FALSE) |
                   str_detect(coalesce(fund_name, ""), "SP|DOW|Dow|DJ") |
                   str_detect(name_lc, dp_index_names),

      # Exchange-traded products
      ETF = coalesce(et_flag == "F", FALSE) | str_detect(name_lc, dp_etf_names),
      ETN = coalesce(et_flag == "N", FALSE) | str_detect(coalesce(fund_name, ""), "ETN") |
            str_detect(name_lc, "exchange traded note|exchange-traded note"),

      # Leveraged / inverse / enhanced
      enhanced = coalesce(index_fund_flag == "E", FALSE) | str_detect(name_lc, dp_enh_names),

      # Target-date funds
      target = reduce(map(seq(2000, 2065, by = 5), \(y) identify_tdf(coalesce(fund_name, ""), y)),
                      `|`) == 1
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: pipeline

steps <- list()
log_step <- function(label, d, unit) {
  steps[[length(steps) + 1]] <<- tibble(step = label, unit = unit,
                                        n_obs = nrow(d), n_funds = n_distinct(d$wficn))
}

style_cols <- c("lipper_class", "lipper_obj_cd", "si_obj_cd", "wbrger_obj_cd", "crsp_obj_cd")

# 0. Raw
d <- fund_raw
log_step("0. Raw file (2000+, year-end, TNA non-missing)", d, "share-class-years")

# 1. Style codes: drop funds that never have a Lipper or CRSP objective code
d <- d |>
  mutate(across(all_of(style_cols), blank_to_na)) |>
  mutate(no_style = all(is.na(lipper_obj_cd) & is.na(crsp_obj_cd)), .by = crsp_fundno) |>
  filter(!no_style) |>
  select(-no_style)
log_step("1. Drop funds with no style code in any year", d, "share-class-years")

# 2. Fill missing style codes: carry the last known code forward, then back-fill the start
d <- d |>
  arrange(crsp_fundno, year) |>
  group_by(crsp_fundno) |>
  fill(all_of(style_cols), .direction = "downup") |>
  ungroup()

# 3. Flag types, then remove ETNs, leveraged/inverse funds, and target-date funds
d <- flag_types(d)
d <- d |> filter(!(ETN | enhanced | target))
log_step("2. Drop ETNs, leveraged/inverse, target-date funds", d, "share-class-years")

# 4. Domestic equity for at least 50% of a fund's observations, then keep those years
d <- d |>
  mutate(share_dom = mean(domestic_equity), .by = crsp_fundno) |>
  filter(share_dom >= 0.5, domestic_equity)
log_step("3. Domestic equity (CRSP/Lipper codes; no foreign names; >= 50% of years)", d, "share-class-years")

# 5. Drop active ETFs (ETF flag but not passive); label the three vehicle types
d <- d |>
  filter(!(ETF & !index_fund)) |>
  mutate(fund_type = case_when(ETF ~ "ETF", index_fund ~ "Index", TRUE ~ "Active"))
log_step("4. Drop active ETFs; label Active / Index / ETF", d, "share-class-years")

# 6. Aggregate share classes to the fund (WFICN) level
d <- d |>
  mutate(exp_ratio_clean = if_else(exp_ratio == -99 | exp_ratio > 0.1, NA_real_, exp_ratio)) |>
  mutate(fund_first_offer = min(first_offer_dt, na.rm = TRUE), .by = wficn)   # oldest share class

fund_year <- d |>
  summarise(
    fund_type      = mode_chr(fund_type),
    lipper_obj_cd  = mode_chr(lipper_obj_cd),
    true_type      = mode_chr(true_type),
    total_tna      = sum(tna_latest, na.rm = TRUE),
    exp_ratio      = weighted.mean(exp_ratio_clean, tna_latest, na.rm = TRUE),
    first_offer_dt = first(fund_first_offer),
    caldt          = max(caldt),
    n_classes      = n(),
    .by = c(wficn, year)
  ) |>
  mutate(fund_age = time_length(caldt - first_offer_dt, unit = "year"))
log_step("5. Aggregate share classes to funds (WFICN-years)", fund_year, "fund-years")

# 7. Incubation: drop the first three years of a fund's life (DP 2026)
fund_year <- fund_year |> filter(fund_age >= 3)
log_step("6. Drop first 3 years of life (incubation bias)", fund_year, "fund-years")

# 8. Size: drop fund-years with TNA below $15 million
fund_year <- fund_year |> filter(total_tna >= 15)
log_step("7. Drop TNA below $15 million", fund_year, "fund-years")

# 9. Missing or invalid expense ratio (DP 2026)
fund_year <- fund_year |> filter(!is.na(exp_ratio), is.finite(exp_ratio))
log_step("8. Drop missing / invalid expense ratio", fund_year, "fund-years")

attrition <- bind_rows(steps)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-attrition
#| tbl-cap: "Sample attrition after each filter (this run)"

attrition |>
  mutate(pct_funds = n_funds / first(n_funds)) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(n_obs, n_funds), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = pct_funds, decimals = 0) |>
  cols_label(step = "Step", unit = "Unit", n_obs = "Observations",
             n_funds = "Funds (WFICN)", pct_funds = "% of raw funds") |>
  tab_header(title = "How Many Funds Survive Each Filter?",
             subtitle = "Simulated CRSP-style panel")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-attrition
#| fig-cap: "Number of distinct funds remaining after each filter"

hchart(attrition, "column", hcaes(x = step, y = n_funds)) |>
  hc_chart(height = 420) |>
  hc_title(text = "Funds remaining after each filter") |>
  hc_xAxis(title = list(text = NULL),
           labels = list(style = list(fontSize = "9px"), rotation = -35)) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Distinct funds (WFICN)")) |>
  hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>
  hc_plotOptions(column = list(dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "{y:,.0f}"))) |>
  hc_tooltip(pointFormat = "<b>{point.y:,.0f}</b> funds")
```
